subject: paediatrics
title: Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Surfactant and Wet Lung

steps.tx: The leading cause of respiratory failure in premature infants is **neonatal respiratory distress syndrome**, historically termed hyaline membrane disease. Arising almost exclusively in infants born before thirty-four weeks gestation, the primary pathophysiological defect is developmental deficiency of pulmonary surfactant, leading to widespread microatelectasis and progressive ventilatory failure.
steps.say: Respiratory distress syndrome is caused by developmental surfactant deficiency in premature infants.

vis.alt: Placental transfer of antenatal corticosteroids stimulating fetal alveolar surfactant synthesis.
vis.caption: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome: chest X-ray with diffuse reticulogranular pattern and air bronchograms beside an infant with nasal flaring. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Pulmonary surfactant is synthesized, packaged in lamellar bodies, and secreted by **alveolar type two pneumocytes**. Composed of eighty percent phospholipids, ten percent neutral lipids, and ten percent proteins, its primary active component is dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine. Surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension at end-expiration, preventing alveolar collapse in accordance with the Law of Laplace.
steps.say: Surfactant synthesized by type two pneumocytes lowers surface tension to prevent end-expiratory collapse.

rows: Forms compact monolayer reducing surface tension to zero
Promotes rapid spreading of surfactant over alveolar surface
Hydrophilic collectins mediating innate immune defense

steps.tx: In the absence of functional surfactant, high surface tension causes **widespread alveolar collapse**. Diffuse microatelectasis results in right-to-left intrapulmonary shunting, severe ventilation-perfusion mismatch, hypoxia, and respiratory acidosis. Epithelial damage and transudation of fibrinogen into alveolar spaces form eosinophilic fibrin-rich hyaline membranes that severely impair diffusion.
steps.say: High surface tension causes alveolar collapse, intrapulmonary shunting, and hyaline membrane formation.

steps.tx: The diagnostic radiological appearance on chest radiography is a **diffuse reticulogranular ground glass pattern**. High surface tension produces uniform microatelectasis appearing as fine granular opacities distributed symmetrically throughout both lung fields. Concurrently, patent major bronchi stand out prominently as dark branching air bronchograms against the opacified background, while overall lung volume is markedly reduced.
steps.say: Chest radiography displays diffuse reticulogranular ground-glass opacities with prominent air bronchograms.

rows: Mild distress responding to CPAP alone

steps.tx: A vital preventive intervention in threatened preterm labor is maternal **antenatal corticosteroid administration**. Intramuscular betamethasone administered as two twelve-milligram doses twenty-four hours apart between twenty-four and thirty-four weeks gestation crosses the placenta to bind fetal glucocorticoid receptors, accelerating alveolar maturation and cutting RDS incidence and neonatal mortality in half.
steps.say: Antenatal betamethasone accelerates lung maturation and cuts respiratory distress syndrome by half.

left.title: Recommended Regimens
points: Betamethasone: 12 mg IM every 24 hours (2 doses)
Dexamethasone: 6 mg IM every 12 hours (4 doses)

right.title: Proven Clinical Reductions
points: Reduces overall neonatal mortality by 40 percent

steps.tx: Prevention of respiratory distress in a threatened preterm birth is maternal **antenatal corticosteroid administration**. Betamethasone 12 mg intramuscularly, two doses 24 hours apart, between 24 and 34 weeks, crosses the placenta, binds fetal glucocorticoid receptors, speeds alveolar maturation, and cuts both respiratory distress syndrome and neonatal death by about half. If the infant is still preterm and working to breathe, early nasal CPAP through binasal prongs at about five to eight centimetres of water keeps alveoli open without an immediate endotracheal tube.
steps.say: Two intramuscular doses of betamethasone, 12 mg and a day apart, given from 24 to 34 weeks, mature the fetal lung and roughly halve respiratory distress and neonatal death. A preterm baby who still struggles can start on nasal CPAP with binasal prongs at five to eight centimetres of water, holding alveoli open before intubation.

vis.alt: A preterm infant receiving early nasal CPAP through binasal prongs at five to eight centimetres of water.
vis.caption: Binasal prongs deliver nasal CPAP at about five to eight centimetres of water to a preterm infant. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The modern delivery room standard for managing spontaneous breathing in preterm infants is **early nasal continuous positive airway pressure**. Applying five to eight centimeters of water pressure via binasal prongs maintains end-expiratory alveolar stability, establishes functional residual capacity, and avoids the barotrauma and volutrauma associated with early invasive endotracheal mechanical ventilation.
steps.say: Early nasal CPAP maintains functional residual capacity and avoids invasive ventilator trauma.

vis.alt: Preterm infant on early nasal CPAP with binasal prongs delivering five to eight centimetres of water pressure
vis.caption: Preterm infant on early nasal CPAP with binasal prongs delivering five to eight centimetres of water pressure. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: When infants on CPAP require rising inspired oxygen fractions exceeding thirty percent, **exogenous surfactant replacement therapy** is administered. Natural bovine or porcine extracts like poractant alfa are instilled directly into the trachea using minimally invasive surfactant administration techniques, rapidly expanding lung compliance and dramatically reducing oxygen and ventilatory requirements.
steps.say: Exogenous surfactant instilled into the trachea improves compliance and reduces oxygen needs.

points: Natural animal extracts superior to synthetics

steps.tx: A common clinical mimic in late preterm infants delivered by elective cesarean is **transient tachypnoea of the newborn**. Arising from delayed resorption of fetal alveolar fluid by epithelial sodium channels, infants present with rapid respirations within hours of birth. Radiography reveals prominent perihilar vascular markings and fluid in interlobar fissures, with spontaneous resolution occurring within forty-eight hours.
steps.say: Transient tachypnoea results from delayed lung fluid clearance and resolves in forty-eight hours.
